checks.subject: Business tool semantics
checks.evidence: Observer passes the original name, arguments and keyword options through. Ordinary contextless reads remain contextless and bind to decrypted dispatched durable in_flight operation/name. Context-bearing reads check task identity; no scope context is manufactured. Actual Q01/Q06 fixture tool responses and candidate mechanical readbacks succeed.

checks.subject: Internal runtime calls
checks.evidence: Runtime-instance internal observer checks actual durable queued proposal and forwards unchanged selected task/start time to original _internal_tool. Actual ryn_update_plan synthetic proposal is accepted with criteria_proposals_accepted=false. No production method implementation changed.

checks.subject: Registration and source ordering
checks.evidence: Fresh exclusive files, actual registration byte SHA, task readback and fsync precede first task bridge/tool call; model-call provenance equals durable model events. Registration drift blocks execution. Collector setup probes explicitly excluded. Existing immutable owner-source and ModelDispatchAdapter checks remain in place.

checks.subject: Reference original RPC and native session
checks.evidence: Node writes/fsyncs metadata-only JSONL before emitting original pipe RPC. Host validates RPC sequence, session/id/method/task/registration/sampling binding before callback. Independent seven-field corruption tests dispatch nothing. Fresh actual pinned-worker fixtures correlate separate native JSONL with host model IDs and read-only SQLite session/messages; database byte SHA independently rechecked.

checks.subject: Failure and incompleteness
checks.evidence: Thrown controller errors or tracked observer faults produce partial_dispatch_collection, including faults swallowed into runtime tool errors. Missing native evidence remains pending; mismatching JSONL/session remains failed with no observed request IDs. Capture exclusive creation prevents resuming/relabeling an old output. These labels concern capture completeness, not model/business success.

checks.subject: No metadata leakage or activation
checks.evidence: Audit stores IDs/times/hashes and tool name; original model messages/specs and business arguments contain no run_nonce. Pinned engine config provenance is out-of-band. New fixture kind stays local-role-query-v2-draft, effective input disabled/not_formal_ready, formal_trial_registered=false. v1 normalizer rejects v2 kind. No full grader or formal dependency pass is asserted.

checks.evidence: All author frozen hashes, author fixture artifacts and four retained failed/intermediate fixture run hashes were rechecked unchanged. Author implementation record retains the initial green-test coverage gap and its tool-context regression; reviewer has not upgraded those runs.

limitations: No real or paid API calls were made; fixture success is collection and control-flow evidence, not Q01/Q06 model-semantic success or overall acceptance.
Hashes/times and sidecar linkage rely on trusted local collectors; no adversarial-host attestation, independent external facts, or two-host transport proof.

Native worker RPC IDs are original worker pipe sequence IDs, not upstream SDK request IDs or fields persisted in the native SQLite schema. SQLite session existence/message count and sidecar request association are separately scoped evidence.

Audit events are bridge/gateway attempts and may precede budget, permission or upstream refusal; they do not assert token consumption or successful execution. Setup probes are outside this task-dispatch scope.

Successful native JSONL/session validation does not itself assess answer truth, role correctness or security dependencies. Missing native evidence remains separately pending even where host capture is complete.
Scoped to fresh single-task Q01/Q06 draft controller; no recovery/resume guarantee, no coverage claim for arbitrary write/reconcile workflows, no v2 normalizer implementation or formal activation.
No historical sample acquired new dispatch evidence; old records remain at their original evidence strength.
